title: Quake - SRP (Slop Rust Port)
author: zasff
selftext:
Play it here (shareware version):

*  [https://quake-srp.pages.dev/](https://quake-srp.pages.dev/)

Source code here:

* [https://github.com/terrapapagalli1516/quake-srp](https://github.com/terrapapagalli1516/quake-srp)

Made by AI with human assistance.

This is a port of the original Quake source code from C to Rust (WinQuake, to be specific, the software renderer); i.e. everything is rendered on the CPU, across multiple cores (for good and bad).

Includes several QoL improvements over the original game: torches that flicker (they look so nice omg), smooth animations, high frame rates, widescreen, touch-screen controls.

The video is slop as well: I was about to share the game, asked for a video in passing, and the results were jaw-dropping. I got a bit desensitized as we kept iterating, but it's still crazy how good models are with video (and in general) these days.

This first release probably contains some bugs: mouse sensitivity might be too low on some machines (adjustable in the options menu); the default brightness is also a bit on the low side in some cases (also adjustable in the options menu).
